title: FAUST. X. Formaldehyde in the protobinary system [BHB2007] 11: Small-scale deuteration
question: Constrain the deuterium fractionation ratios in formaldehyde (H2CO, HDCO, and D2CO) at small spatial scales in the Class 0/I protobinary system [BHB2007] 11 and investigate the kinematics of its extended emission.

data.bands: Band 6 (FAUST also observed Band 3, but only Band 6 is analysed here)
data.arrays: 12 m main array and 7 m ACA

what.value: Spectroscopic parameters (frequency, partition function, Einstein coefficient, upper level energy, upper level degeneracy) from CDMS and JPL databases

evidence.quote: Frequency ($\nu$ in Hz), partition function (Q($T_{\rm ex}$)), Einstein coefficient ($A_{\rm ul}$), energy of the upper level ($E_{\rm u}$ in K) and upper level population ($g_{\rm u}$) are taken from the Cologne Database for Molecular Spectroscopy (CDMS; (cite: muller01)).
Based on analysis carried out with the CASSIS software ((cite: Vastel2015)) and JPL (http://spec.jpl.nasa.gov/) and CDMS (https://cdms.astro.uni-koeln.de/classic/) molecular databases.
[BHB2007] 11 is a Class 0/I protostellar core ((cite: brooke), (cite: forbrich), (cite: sandell)) located 163 $\pm$ 5 pc away ((cite: dzib)) in the Barnard 59 (B59) core.

what.value: Central mass of the system for kinematic streamer modelling

evidence.quote: Along with the central mass of the system (taken from (cite: vastel)), the input parameters for the model are the spherical co-ordinates of the initial position and radial velocity of this parcel of mass within a cloud

what.value: Disk inclination angle i and disk position angle (138 deg)

evidence.quote: The axis of the extension seems to be aligned with that seen in the continuum, which has a position angle of 138$\degree$ ((cite: Alves17))

In order to obtain the position and velocity values with respect to the observer, two rotations are applied due to the inclination angle *i* and the disk position angle (both taken from (cite: Alves17)).

what.value: Bolometric luminosity of the source (1.68 x 10^27 W)

evidence.quote: $L_{\rm bol}$ represents the bolometric luminosity of the source (taken as $1.68\times10^{27}$ W - (cite: sandell)), all in cgs units.

what.value: CH3OH velocity components (-2, 2.8 and 9.9 km s^-1) and 2D deconvolution source sizes

evidence.quote: also shows dashed lines denoting the three velocity components first identified in CH$_3$OH emission towards \[BHB2007\] 11 as described in (cite: vastel) at -2, 2.8 and 9.9 km s$^{-1}$
These findings agree with the 2D deconvolution presented in (cite: vastel) in that the component associated with Source A is slightly more extended than those associated with Source B.

recipe.goal: Create moment maps and extract source spectra
recipe.method: Analyse clean maps in GILDAS, identify line channels to create moment 0 and moment 1 maps combining 12 m and 7 m configurations, define an extraction polygon from the 4-sigma contour of the HDCO 259 GHz transition, extract spectra in Jy and convert to synthesised beam temperature (K) in GILDAS/CLASS.
key_parameters: 4-sigma contour of HDCO 259 GHz map used as extraction polygon
Velocity integration ranges for H2CO components: -5 to 0 km s^-1, 1 to 8 km s^-1, 8 to 15 km s^-1; extended structure: 0 to 6 km s^-1
Continuum offset of 10.3 K added to H2CO spectrum to model absorption; baseline offset of 0.1 K corrected in HDCO 259 GHz spectrum

recipe.goal: Measure emitting component sizes via 2D image deconvolution
recipe.method: Run 2D Gaussian deconvolution on the peak emission channel of each of the three velocity components in both HDCO transitions (excluding the blended component of HDCO 4(1,4)-3(1,3)) using CASA imfit.

recipe.goal: Perform LTE radiative transfer modelling and derive column densities and D/H ratios
recipe.method: Fit Gaussian line profiles using Levenberg-Marquardt fitting and perform LTE radiative transfer MCMC modelling in CASSIS to derive V_LSR, FWHM, T_ex, and total column densities (N_TOT) for HDCO, H2CO, and D2CO, then compute D/H = 0.5 * N(HDCO)/N(H2CO).
key_parameters: Emitting sizes for beam dilution correction: lower limit 0.15" (Source B) and 0.50" (Source A); upper limit 0.30" (Source B) and 1.00" (Source A)
Fixed T_ex = 90 K for H2CO and D2CO emission components (and blended HDCO component); T_ex = 13 K (or <13 K) for envelope absorption
Background temperature T_bg = 2.73 K (CMB); calibration uncertainty = 10%
assumptions: Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium (LTE) conditions and a common origin of disk emission across H2CO, HDCO, and CH3OH
Uniform H2CO emission across the extraction region where HDCO is emitting

recipe.goal: Map centroid velocities and model extended kinematics with a free-fall streamer model
recipe.method: Perform pixel-by-pixel Gaussian fitting on H2CO (between 0 and 6 km s^-1, split at 3.5 km s^-1) using pyspeckit for pixels >= 5-sigma, define polygons excluding high-velocity disk emission, and compare sky trajectories and velocity-distance profiles against an analytic free-falling streamline model.
key_parameters: Velocity intervals: 3.5 to 6 km s^-1 (redshifted lobe) and 0 to 3.5 km s^-1 (blueshifted lobe); minimum intensity threshold of 5-sigma
Model parameters: initial distance r_0, radial velocity v_r,0, position angle theta_0, azimuthal angle phi_0, angular velocity Omega_0, central mass, inclination i, disk PA = 138 deg
assumptions: Material is free-falling with conserved angular momentum towards the central mass

score_reason: The ALMA project code, spectral transitions, software tools (CASA 5.6.1-8, GILDAS/CLASS, CASSIS, pyspeckit), and LTE fitting parameters/assumptions (Table 3) are clearly documented, allowing close reproduction of the radiative transfer and D/H results once spectra are extracted. However, the custom FAUST self-calibration/combination details, exact polygon coordinates, and numerical parameters of the kinematic streamer model are not stated.
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA Large Program data (2018.1.01205.L) with well-defined transitions and quantitative column density and D/H targets in Table 3 that can be re-derived from the combined cubes.
